🖥 Iran to use nuclear technology to control disease-carrying mosquitoes

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) and the Ministry of Health have signed an agreement to use nuclear technology to control disease-carrying mosquitoes, including the Aedes aegypti species.

AEOI Chief Mohammad Eslami and Health Minister Mohammad-Reza Zafarghandi signed the agreement on Sunday to expand the use of nuclear technology in healthcare.
​
Under the agreement, the two sides will establish a facility for mass-rearing sterile male Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and conduct laboratory and field trials to assess the effectiveness of the technology.
​
The method involves using radiation to sterilize male mosquitoes before releasing them into targeted areas to reduce successful reproduction and gradually suppress mosquito populations.
​
The AEOI will support the project by providing gamma or X-ray irradiation equipment, training personnel, supplying specialists in irradiation and dosimetry, and ensuring the proper operation and maintenance of the equipment.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian, in a telephone conversation with the Sultan of Oman, has emphasized the importance of bilateral cooperation and constructive consultations aimed at consolidating regional peace and stability.

In the phone call on Sunday, Pezeshkian extended birthday greetings to Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, wishing the government and people of Oman continued prosperity and success.
​
Pezeshkian commended the Sultan and the Omani government for their efforts to promote regional peace and stability. He stressed the importance of maintaining diplomatic consultations, expanding constructive interactions, and utilizing the shared potential of regional nations to foster mutual understanding and cooperation.
​
Highlighting the friendly, long-standing ties between Iran and Oman, the President invited Sultan Haitham to visit Tehran, expressing hope that arrangements for an in-person meeting would be made soon.
​
In response, the Sultan expressed gratitude for the congratulatory message and reaffirmed Oman’s consistent policy of supporting peace and stability in the region.
​
He noted that close communication and consultation with Iran remain a priority for his country. Sultan Haitham also thanked Pezeshkian for the invitation, stating that the visit would take place at a suitable time.

⚡️ President Pezeshkian highlights unity as key to building stronger Iran

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian has called on Iranians to support one another and set aside divisions, saying national solidarity would help the country grow stronger across scientific, social and humanitarian fields.

Pezeshkian made the remarks on Sunday at an event titled Smile of the Homeland, held to mark National Children’s Week, where the president used a familiar childhood story to explain the power of unity.
​
Holding two sticks, he recalled a story from schoolbooks about a father who, nearing the end of his life, called his children together. He gave them a single stick and asked them to break it, which they did easily. He then bundled several sticks together and challenged them to break the bundle, but none could.
​
Addressing the children at the ceremony, Pezeshkian asked why the bundle had proved impossible to break.
​
When sticks came together, they could not break it, he explained, drawing a lesson about solidarity.
​
The president said Iranians should be friends, help one another and offer mutual support to build a powerful and resilient country capable of making progress in every field.
​
He stressed that cooperation should extend to scientific advancement, service to others and treating people with humanity.
​
Pezeshkian said the story had come back to him from his childhood and that its message remained relevant: unity creates strength, while internal conflict gives adversaries an opportunity to inflict harm.
​
He urged people to stand together and move forward with determination, adding that enemies should not be emboldened to attack Iran.
​
At the sidelines of the event, two children presented Pezeshkian with a plaque in appreciation of his efforts.
